newsitem.title: UK: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.
newsitem.headline: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.

text.p: LONDON, Feb 19 Reuter) - A total 17,000 tonnes of current series white sugar received export rebates of a maximum 44.008 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos at Wednesday's European Union (EU) tender, the U.K. Intervention Board said.
Traders in France received all the tonnage, it added.

This week's award brings the cumulative tonnage awarded for export from the 1996/97 crop to 1.533 million tonnes. This compares with the 3,500 tonnes awarded on February 21, 1996, when the cumulative tonnage totalled 1.60 million tonnes.
Earlier on Wednesday, London traders had expected the subsidy for the current season whites campaign for licences to end-July to be between 44.008 and 44.028 Ecus per 100 kilos.
Traders had also forecast the total authorised sugar tonnage export awards to be between 30,000 and 60,000 tonnes versus 96,500 last week when the restitution was 44.787 Ecus.
